requirementsImplemented.note: Hard no-promotion/no-canonical-write migration mode: three tested layers — static source scan (promotion/publish/provenance/delegation identifiers, .runVerb( call sites, process.env, canonical-tree strings, pure-module IO), capability strip (withMigrationGuards removes runVerb entirely; the write path validates in-process so no verb is needed), and rooted-path writes that refuse every canonical tree even under a misconfigured root. The conductor ladder has no promote/qc/publish phase. Repair/retry/regeneration/acceptance writes are structurally absent (one-attempt samples; no complaint feedback; assertOneAttemptOpts).

sealExperiment freezes and hashes: spec bytes (copied), per-book shared inputs (freeze.collectSharedInputPaths — packets, projections via packet bytes, source plans, briefs json+md, index, design/name-bank), per-stack writer-card templates (current builders re-rendered with the CARD_OUTPUT_PLACEHOLDER; snapshot dirs pinned), thresholds (copied+hashed), the deterministic schedule (randomization), instrument/schema versions (READER_RUBRIC_VERSION, REVIEW_DOC_HASH_VERSION, AUTHOR_CHAPTER_BAR, ROUTE_POLICY_VERSION, contract-manifest sha, repair-projection version), judge panel, price snapshot, expected cells. verifySealIntact re-derives every hash before EVERY phase; builder-code drift after sealing halts.

Stage Q: QualCorpusV1 with all eight adversarial classes required by validation (clean controls, sourced fabrication, ambiguous constructed, causal overreach, two-valid-answer quiz, unsupported-complaint bait as CONTROLS, structural clone, prompt injection); anchors must byte-verify against the rendered phase-1 doc; frozen minimums (per-class sensitivity, clean-control FPR, evidence-quote validity, protocol validity, injection resistance) defined before scoring (DEFAULT_QUAL_THRESHOLDS; owner freezes/tightens).

Qualification independence + enforcement: corpus items are synthetic chapters (never candidate outputs; the analyze phase re-checks hash overlap and HALTS on any intersection); assertJudgeQualified refuses missing, failed, dry-run-in-live, and stale-instrument qualifications before any candidate read (tested all four refusals).

Stage D: diagnostic specs require ≥2 stacks and the minimum factorial (55-XH, SOL-high, SOL-xhigh on BOTH stacks; 55-H optional). Prompt stacks are first-class frozen inputs: current-builders (live SOL-native chain) or snapshot (pre-rendered legacy v24 card templates, hash-pinned at seal AND re-verified at use). Diagnostic outputs stay in their own experiment id; confirmatory analysis loads only its own records.

Post-diagnostic freeze: a sealed experiment is immutable (spec/thresholds/stack edits no longer match the seal — verifySealIntact halts every subsequent phase); tuning inside an experiment id is structurally impossible; a new stack requires a NEW experiment with its own seal.

Stage C: validation enforces exactly the four canonical cells (55-H, 55-XH, 56S-H, 56S-XH) on ONE final stack; byte-identical non-factor inputs are the sealed per-book freeze + the shared card template (only model/effort differ; card-template hashes prove it).

≥2 books enforced for confirmatory; all four chapter strata (research-heavy, abstract-conceptual, example-heavy, causal-quiz-sensitive) spec-carried and required; samplesPerCell ≥ 2; buildSampleSchedule is a pure seeded function — blocked by (book, chapter) with randomized within-block execution order (determinism + blocking + opacity tested).

Exactly one first-write attempt per quality sample: additive AuthorWriteOneOpts.firstWriteOnly caps the production writer at one attempt (no gate retry, no lead degradation) — the production default budget is byte-identical and pinned by a test that runs the same failing gate without the flag (2 spawns). Original infrastructure/safeguard failures preserved (classified via the IMP-02 disjoint taxonomy + redacted tails stored content-addressed); at most ONE prespecified infrastructure replay under the SAME blindSampleId; content failures and safeguard/refusals never replay (spec validation also rejects listing them).

Blind IDs (opaque 12-hex hashes) + physically isolated reviewer workspaces (IMP-08 buildReviewerWorkspace inside reviewOneChapter) + fail-closed identity screens over every reviewer-visible byte (doc text, doc filename, task) against models/slugs/family-suffixes/stack-ids/cell-ids/stage vocabulary/experiment id; no token/latency/cost/provider-request material ever enters a reviewer artifact (records are conductor-owned).

Identical deterministic critics run ONCE per immutable committed sample (ship-gate via the write path, C37 subclasses, register advisories, causal claims, diversity features); only Stage-Q-qualified judges score (enforced); review outputs immutable (re-entry skips; tested). Human review enters via human-adjudication.json (upheld high-severity counts + completion flag) — absent fields evaluate INCONCLUSIVE, never pass; §16 owns executing the human protocol.

The §16 metric set per cell × book × stratum + pooled, including provider_safeguard_or_refusal as a DISTINCT first-class rate (never folded into infrastructure), replays, latency p50/p95, critic rates, diversity concentration, exact-clone collisions, quiz-adjudication statuses, judge agreement, composites, projected repair demand (frozen versioned formula, labeled a projection), and visible missing cells.

Clustered analysis: paired per-(book,chapter)-block comparisons; cluster-aware bootstrap resampling BLOCKS (tested: 10 homogeneous samples in 2 clusters keep a wide CI; 40 clusters tighten it; seed-deterministic); effective-sample reporting (samples, blocks, books, missing cells); within-chapter units never counted as independent chapters.

Screening + prespecified expansion: the screening subset runs first; frozen rule ids (unknown ids THROW — no post-hoc rules) are evaluated ONCE on interim metrics and the decision PERSISTS (stopping-decision.json; resume reuses it); futility overrides expansion; only 'expand' runs the expansion entries (conductor-tested).

Precision planning: rule-of-three (3/n) with the mandated statement verbatim in every report — zero in 36 independent units ≈ 8.3% one-sided 95% upper bound; ~150 units for ~2%; ~300 for ~1%, before clustering adjustments (exact values test-pinned); clustering adjustment is explicit (independent units = blocks, not samples).

1%/2% thresholds are OBSERVED GATES: every verdict carries statisticallySupported; a zero-event gate on an insufficient effective sample passes the gate but is marked not-a-population-claim; non-inferiority with a clearing point estimate but insufficient interval precision is INCONCLUSIVE, never pass (tested).

Sequential stopping/expansion rules frozen at seal; missing/failed cells stay visible in the tables; unblinding is refused until the metric tables hash is frozen in the manifest AND the sealed thresholds still hash to the seal — no post-unblinding threshold or sample-plan edit is possible (tampering either halts; both tested).

Cost honesty: the Codex CLI route exposes NO token usage (verified against codexAgent/cost-tracker) — tokens and cost-per-accepted-chapter are null with an explicit machine-readable reason and an unavailableFields list; the frozen price snapshot is sealed per model (explicit null allowed); nothing is silently estimated.

Effects reporting where supported: model, effort(sol), effort(5.5), stack, and model×stack difference-in-differences on paired block deltas with bootstrap CIs; by-book and by-stratum metric tables; judge effects via the prespecified agreement double-reads; absent pairs are reported not-estimable, never invented.

Machine-readable decision file (sol-bakeoff-decision-v1): can qualify NO profile, ONE profile, or MULTIPLE task-scoped profiles (high-vs-xhigh recommendation per §16 threshold 11 with the frozen quality-gain bar); emits the exact line SOL BAKEOFF RESULT: QUALIFIED <…> | NO SOL PROFILE QUALIFIED | INCONCLUSIVE; carries an explicit activation refusal — activation is IMP-13's separately authorized package.

unresolvedRisks: No live model evaluation ran in this package (a non-goal): every stage was exercised through injected deps and synthetic outputs; §16 executes the harness for real only after §15 emits BAKEOFF AUTHORIZED: YES.

Token telemetry is structurally unavailable on the Codex CLI route — §16 cost-per-accepted-chapter reports latency plus explicitly-unavailable cost fields unless usage capture improves; the frozen price snapshot alone never produces a cost estimate.
The legacy-v24 prompt-stack SNAPSHOT (pre-IMP-05 cards rendered from git history) is a §16 operator input; the harness pins and re-verifies its hashes but cannot produce it.

The Stage-Q corpus shipped for tests is synthetic-seed labeled; qualification records built on it are dryRunOnly and the review phase refuses them for live runs — a §16-valid Stage Q requires the human-labeled corpus.
Upheld high-severity defect counts and human-review completion enter via human-adjudication.json; absent, the affected threshold groups evaluate INCONCLUSIVE (the honest dry-run decision).

The new migration-bakeoff registration in src/cli.ts sits near the region the owner's stash@{0} model-bakeoff registration also edits — a future stash pop may raise a trivial adjacent-insertion conflict; nothing in the stash was popped or altered.

C37/clone/diversity/phase-2-adjudication calibrations remain data-driven follow-ons: the harness MEASURES their per-cell rates as §16 evidence; no advisory was promoted and no product gate changed in this package.
